design.purpose: Isolate bias caused by assuming beta_aer(ref)=0 when a broad smooth aerosol contribution preserves an approximately molecular Rayleigh-window shape.

correct_boundary_check: Using the true beta_total(ref)=beta_m(ref)+beta_aer(ref) recovers the lower-column synthetic truth to numerical accuracy (relative L2 approximately 2e-5 at 355 nm and 1e-6 at 532 nm over the sweep).
interpretation: A broad smooth aerosol residual can pass the existing Rayleigh-window slope/variance/valid-fraction QA while materially violating the productive aerosol-free boundary assumption.
At 532 nm in this controlled case, f=0.10 produces about 8% lower-column L2 bias and 10% integrated-column underestimation; f=0.20 produces about 15% and 19%; f=0.50 produces about 31% and 39%.
The wavelength dependence of the bias is physical/model-dependent; these numerical values are a controlled mechanism test, not operational thresholds.
Correct boundary knowledge removes the bias, confirming that the failure is the boundary condition rather than the Fernald implementation.
decision: Boundary residual aerosol must become an explicit R&D dimension. Existing Rayleigh shape QA cannot be treated as proof that beta_aer(ref)=0.
